headline: Data Centers Pay Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, such as data centers, to bear more of the costs associated with their grid infrastructure demands, potentially reducing residential utility bills.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, environmental groups, Senator L. Louise Lucas
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users
news_headline: Virginia bill aims to cut residential energy costs by shifting expenses to data centers
news_summary: A Virginia bill, similar to HB 1393, aims to shift energy costs for increased generating capacity to data centers and other large energy users consuming 25 MW or more, potentially saving residential customers over $65 annually. This legislation seeks to address the growing energy demand from data centers, which currently account for about 20% of Dominion Energy's sales.

headline: Data Center Water Use Transparency
short_summary: This bill mandates waterworks operators to categorize and report water consumption data, including that of data centers, to the State Water Control Board, increasing transparency regarding their environmental footprint.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservation advocates, State Sen. Kannan Srinivasan
news_headline: New regulations beef up data centers' required water use reporting in Virginia
news_summary: New Virginia regulations, effective January 2027, will require waterworks operators to categorize and report monthly water sales data, including usage by data centers, to the State Water Control Board. This bill, carried by State Sen. Kannan Srinivasan, aims to increase transparency regarding data center water consumption, especially crucial during extended drought periods in Virginia.

headline: Local Control Over Data Center Siting
short_summary: This bill grants localities more authority over where data centers can be built and sets requirements for site assessments, including sound profiles, addressing community concerns about noise and environmental impact.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local governments, community groups, residential property owners, Del. Thomas
opponents: Data center industry, economic development agencies
news_headline: Data center noise irks Virginia neighbors: 'You just want to curse'
news_summary: HB 153 introduces new siting requirements for large data centers, mandating impact assessments on noise for nearby residential units and schools, and allowing localities to examine effects on water, agriculture, and historic sites. This legislation reflects growing community concerns over noise pollution from data centers, which has become a significant issue for residents living near these facilities.
